one_liner: @noble/hashes 1.8.0 drop-in with SHA-2, SHA-1, MD5, PBKDF2 and scrypt in WebAssembly; 1.7-7.8x faster than noble's JS.
what_it_does: A copy of @noble/hashes 1.8.0 in which the compression functions of SHA-256/224, the SHA-512 family, SHA-1 and MD5, PBKDF2's iteration loop and scrypt's ROMix run in WebAssembly; every other module (SHA-3, BLAKE, RIPEMD-160, Argon2, HKDF) is noble's file byte for byte. Exports, errors, callbacks and even instance fields match noble, and it must be installed under the original name ("@noble/hashes": "npm:@r1ck404/fast-noble-hashes@1.8.2") because noble's utils.js imports @noble/hashes/crypto by name. Since 1.8.2, in Node with process.getBuiltinModule, one-shot hashes of at least 64 KiB go to node:crypto instead of the WASM kernels.
how_it_is_fast: The kernels are fully unrolled WASM (SHA-256 8.8 KB, SHA-512 11.3 KB) with state and message words in locals, expanded on first use from 244-541-byte templates written with an in-repo assembler (wasm/kernels.mjs, wasm/asm.mjs). SHA-512 uses native i64 arithmetic where noble's JS splits every 64-bit word into two 32-bit halves, which is why SHA-512/384 gain 5x while SHA-256 gains only 1.7x (V8's JIT already does 32-bit rotates well). One-shot hashers skip instance creation and UTF-8 encode strings straight into WASM memory; PBKDF2 runs all c iterations of HMAC inside WASM from the precomputed inner/outer states; scrypt's ROMix runs salsa20/8 on SIMD v128 registers (wasm/scrypt.wat).
when_to_use: Browser or in-browser-runtime code pinned to @noble/hashes 1.8.x that hashes large buffers with SHA-512/384 (npm lockfile SRI: 5.4x in Node, 6.0x in Chromium), MD5 (7.8x / 5.7x) or SHA-1 (2.6x / 4.3x), where node:crypto is not available.
PBKDF2 key derivation in the browser or in a crypto polyfill: PBKDF2-SHA512 c=10000 7.2x (8.2x in Chromium), PBKDF2-SHA256 3.4x; scrypt N=2^14, r=8 2.3x.
Many short one-shot hashes (56-character strings: 4-7x) such as cache keys or content IDs.
Dependency trees where several packages import @noble/hashes 1.x: one npm alias or pnpm override redirects every import, with no call-site changes.
when_not_to_use: Projects on @noble/hashes 2.x (2.4.0 is current; ESM-only, .js import paths, no string inputs): there is no matching version, and the 1.8.0 baseline also predates noble's own 2.3.0 speedups (+10-45% on 32-byte inputs, +20% PBKDF2/HKDF).
Node server code hashing large buffers: call node:crypto (OpenSSL) or WebCrypto directly; the package itself now defers to node:crypto for one-shot inputs of 64 KiB or more.
SHA-3/Keccak, BLAKE2/BLAKE3, RIPEMD-160 or Argon2: these run noble's unchanged JS (1.0x); hash-wasm or awasm-noble accelerate them.
Hosts without WebAssembly SIMD or with a CSP lacking wasm-unsafe-eval: the accelerated functions throw, there is no JS fallback.

Security-critical code that relies on noble's audits: the WASM kernels and patches are an unaudited, weeks-old re-implementation by one author, assured only by its differential and mutation tests; streaming small updates (1.2x) and HMAC on short strings (1.3x) gain little anyway.

integration.form: module (npm package @r1ck404/fast-noble-hashes; noble's ESM and CommonJS entry points, WASM shipped as text templates inside _fast.js)
integration.dependencies: none at run time (binaryen ^132 and esbuild 0.28.2 only to rebuild the kernels)
integration.min_toolchain: WebAssembly SIMD: Node 16.4+, Chrome/Edge 91+, Firefox 89+, Safari 16.4+ (README; the engines field says ^14.21.3 || >=16); the node:crypto path only where process.getBuiltinModule exists
integration.platforms: any WebAssembly host with SIMD (browser suite runs in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, main thread and module worker)
integration.thread_safety: not documented; each hash family keeps one module-level WASM instance (64 KiB, wiped after every call) per JS realm, and every call copies state in and out synchronously, so async PBKDF2/scrypt slices in one realm do not clash and each worker has its own instances
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same exports, digests, errors and instance fields as @noble/hashes 1.8.0 when installed under its name, but it requires WebAssembly SIMD (throws without it), scrypt memory must fit in 4 GiB of WASM memory, pbkdf2Async/scryptAsync yield a different number of event-loop turns, and noble's private constant tables are gone; useless for noble 2.x

gotchas: The published Node rows describe an older code path: they were measured on 2026-09-28, before commit 7df1749 (2026-09-30, 1.8.2) routed one-shot Uint8Array/Buffer inputs of at least 64 KiB and strings of at least 65,536 code units to node:crypto. The repo's bench uses exactly such inputs (1 MB and 64 KB plain Uint8Arrays, npm tarballs), so rerunning it on current code in Node times OpenSSL, not the WASM kernels; the Chromium rows still measure WASM.

The root README summary row (sha512 5x, md5 6.9x, sha1 2.4x, sha256 1.6x, pbkdf2 3.3-5.7x, scrypt 3.1x) is taken from the older 2026-09-27 run (results/noble-hashes-orig_vs_fast-interleaved-2026-09-27T13-31-54-604Z.md), in which the noble baseline itself ran about 1.5x slower than on 2026-09-28 (scrypt 55.30 vs 36.32 ms, sha512 4.4 MB tarball 46.55 vs 30.47 ms) while the fast scrypt barely moved (17.89 vs 16.06 ms): the 3.1x scrypt figure comes from a slow baseline run, and the detailed table gives 2.3x.

npm 1.8.0 (2026-09-27) wraps the WASM init in a /* @__PURE__ */ IIFE (esm/_fast.js line 99), so bundlers drop it and bundled apps silently get noble's JS speed; fixed in f8aa157 (1.8.1). The npm latest 1.8.3 (2026-09-30 19:12 UTC) has no commit in the repository and changes the glue to share one WASM memory across all hash families, reloading round constants on every family switch.
The package LICENSE still says the kernels are re-implemented in Rust (rust/src), but that directory was replaced by WASM templates in f8aa157; only noble's MIT licence applies.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over hash-wasm when existing code or dependencies already call @noble/hashes 1.8 synchronously and you need identical results and instance state with no call-site changes; pick hash-wasm (its own async API, SHA-3, BLAKE3, Argon2 and more in WASM) for new code or other algorithms, and awasm-noble when BLAKE3 throughput is the goal.
verified_claims_summary: First-party run on a Ryzen 7 7800X3D, Node 24.16 and headless Chromium 149, alternating fresh processes and keeping the best of 3 per-process medians, against pure-JS @noble/hashes 1.8.0: sha512 of the 4.4 MB typescript tarball 30.47 vs 5.68 ms (5.4x; 6.0x in Chromium), md5 1 MB 8.95 vs 1.15 ms (7.8x), sha1 1 MB 2.64 vs 1.01 ms (2.6x), sha256 1 MB 3.65 vs 2.12 ms (1.7x; about 494 MB/s in both Node and Chromium, so the WASM kernel, not OpenSSL), PBKDF2-SHA512 c=10000 24.17 vs 3.36 ms (7.2x), scrypt N=2^14 36.32 vs 16.06 ms (2.3x). node:crypto, WebCrypto and hash-wasm were not compared.
status_note: Active but brand new (first npm release 2026-09-27, single author, 1 star, no issues), MIT, installable by npm alias; it mirrors noble 1.8.0 while upstream is at 2.4.0, and the npm latest (1.8.3) is not reproducible from the repository, so pin a version and re-run its differential tests before trusting it with security-relevant hashing.
